extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, attorneys/agents before the USPTO, OED staff, and respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: A final order imposing reciprocal exclusion from practice before the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 based on a state-court exclusion, describing procedural steps, notices, duties of the excluded practitioner, and administrative effects (Customer Numbers/PKI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline identical to the discipline imposed by a duly constituted authority of a State when a practitioner is excluded from the practice of law by that authority; here, Respondent is excluded from practice before the USPTO pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 for violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), predicated upon being excluded from practice by a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO Director (through the OED Director) can request imposition of disciplinary measures identical to state-imposed discipline; the Final Order effectuates that reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity to respond (40 days) under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' must be sent notifying the respondent that a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline has been filed and providing an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to the state discipline based on reasons in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent may contest the imposition by timely filing a response asserting one or more of the regulatory grounds in § 11.24(d)(1). Failure to timely respond is treated as failure to raise a genuine issue of material fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service by certified mail and publication if undeliverable
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order is to be sent by certified mail to the respondent; if the Notice and Order cannot be delivered, the notice must be published in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order documents certified-mail receipt numbers and, when delivery failed, publication dates in the Official Gazette (e.g., May 29, 2018 and June 5, 2018) to effect service by publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to respond results in finding no genuine issue of material fact under § 11.24(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent does not file a response to the Notice and Order, the OED Director/USPTO may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact and that reciprocal exclusion is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states that, 'In light of Respondent's failure to file a response, it is hereby determined that there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and Respondent's exclusion ... is the appropriate discipline.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice of Exclusion in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director is ordered to publish a Notice of Exclusion in the Official Gazette identifying the respondent, registration number, the disciplinary violation (e.g., § 11.804(h)), and the factual predicate for discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice of Exclusion should state the respondent's name, registration number, the fact of exclusion from practice before the USPTO, the regulatory basis, the underlying state disciplinary findings, and reference statutory/regulatory authority (35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies, courts, and the public under § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the states where the respondent is admitted, to courts where the respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order requires dissemination of the disciplinary outcome beyond the Official Gazette to relevant state agencies and courts to ensure awareness of the exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of excluded practitioner under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: An excluded practitioner 'shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order directs the respondent to follow the obligations set forth in § 11.58 (the order references § 11.58 but does not enumerate the duties on the face of the order).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will dissociate the respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure (PKI) certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative disassociation severs the respondent's linkage to Customer Numbers and PKI credentials to prevent further practice/activity tied to those identifiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining or being added to a USPTO Customer Number until reinstated
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent shall not apply for a USPTO Customer Number, obtain a USPTO Customer Number, nor have his name added to a USPTO Customer Number unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit bar on access/use of USPTO customer account mechanisms for the duration of exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority for action (35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: The disciplinary action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orders imposing reciprocal discipline rely on these statutory/regulatory provisions as the legal basis for exclusion and associated procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Underlying types of misconduct serving as predicate for discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The Colorado Supreme Court disbarred the respondent for neglecting matters entrusted to him, engaging in conduct involving dishonesty and misrepresentation, and failing to cooperate in an Attorney Regulation Counsel Investigation (Colorado Disciplinary Proceedings 16-2462 and 16-3149).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These specific misconduct findings (neglect, dishonesty/misrepresentation, failure to cooperate) are examples of state-imposed grounds that can trigger reciprocal discipline before the USPTO when they result in exclusion by the state authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of disciplinary decisions via OED FOIA Reading Room
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions are available for public review at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's FOIA Reading Room (URL provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order directs that disciplinary decisions be made publicly accessible and identifies the OED FOIA Reading Room as the location for review, supporting transparency and public notice.
